column1: # Genesis hygiene patterns.
# Format: label<TAB>flags<TAB>extended-regex
#   flags: any of `i` (case-insensitive) and `b`, or `-` for none.
# `b` means the pattern is precise enough to run over a file grep judges
# binary. Credential shapes carry it: a secret in a .pack or an image is
# exactly as committed as one in a text file. The loose environment
# heuristics do not -- `internal-hostname` alone matches inside
# /usr/bin/git, and a gate that cries wolf on every binary is a gate
# people switch off.
# WHAT A PATTERN HERE SEES, and this is the place to say it because this is
# the file somebody opens when they add a credential shape.
# The rows here are matched BY SHAPE, against the file's text AND a second
# view `hygiene-decode.py` mirrors beside it: every string a JSON escape hid,
# and the file's own content, both NFC-composed with every invisible or
# combining code point removed -- `decoding.normalized()`, the same function
# the digest half's tokeniser calls. Ruled 2026-09-12 on #72, closing what
# this header used to declare as open: a shaped literal broken by a
# zero-width space, or split across an accent's decomposed spelling, used to
# scan clean here while the digest half already caught its shapeless cousin.
# Measured before the close: an AWS-key-shaped literal with a zero-width
# space inside scanned clean; after, it is caught the same as the intact key.
# A row here may declare an EXCEPTION in the sibling `hygiene-exceptions.tsv`
# -- a data-driven carve-out for a form this repository has decided is not
# private (a public forge's own SSH remote), never a loosening of the
# pattern's own shape. See that file's header.
# `scripts/hygiene.sh` fails the build if any tracked file matches any
# pattern here. This file is the only file the scan skips: it is the one
# place forbidden shapes are meant to be written down.
# Add a pattern here, not in the script. Add a case to
# `scripts/seed-hygiene-fault.sh` at the same time, so that every pattern
# has been seen catch something.
# A row's regex is passed to grep with `-e`. A pattern beginning with `-`
# would otherwise be read as an OPTION, and grep would report every row after
# it as absent -- a whole class silently unguarded while the scan prints the
# same green. Seeded, so the hazard has been seen.
# --- environments that are not this repository ---
private-ipv4
internal-hostname
personal-home-path
session-scratchpad-path
ssh-user-at-host
windows-user-path
# --- identifiers from a tracker this repository does not use ---
internal-ticket-id
# --- credentials ---
aws-access-key-id
github-token
slack-token
private-key-block
anthropic-api-key
openai-api-key
assigned-secret
